resources.string: Block apps and pause the phone when the daily limit is reached

Detoxify watches which app opens so blocked apps can be closed immediately, and so the phone can be gated when the daily screen-time limit is reached. Only used for parental controls you set up in the app.

Swap the phone for a few minutes of real connection. Pick one small ritual — the goal is calm, not perfect.

Calm wind-down

• Read aloud together (even 10 minutes counts)
• Listen to soft music or a bedtime playlist
• Dim lights and do slow stretching or “sleepy yoga”
• Guided breathing: in for 4, hold 2, out for 6
• Pack tomorrow’s bag or lay out clothes together

Low-stimulation play

• Draw or color side by side
• Tell a story one sentence at a time, taking turns
• Simple card or board games
• Look at family photos and share memories
• Stargaze from a window or talk about the day’s “rose & thorn”

Connection without a screen

• Snuggle and ask “What was the kindest thing you saw today?”
• Rub backs or trace letters on their hand to guess
• Hum a lullaby or sing softly
• Whisper a short gratitude list — three tiny good things
• Plan a weekend adventure on paper

Make it easier

• Charge phones outside the bedroom so the habit is shared
• Model putting your own device away first
• Offer two choices (“Book or bath first?”) so they still feel in control
• If they push back, stay kind and brief — consistency beats length
Your brain likes a calm ending to the day. Try one tiny thing with a grown-up — no phone needed.

Wind down

• Listen to a story someone reads to you
• Hum a quiet song together
• Do “lazy lion” stretches: reach up high, then hang loose
• Count slow breaths to ten
• Pick tomorrow’s clothes like a game

Play without a screen

• Draw a silly creature and have a grown-up add to it
• Build a fort from pillows and a blanket
• Play “I spy” in your room
• Make shadow puppets with a flashlight
• Tell a made-up story one word at a time

Together time

• Ask a grown-up about their favorite day when they were your age
• Share your “best moment” and “tricky moment” from today
• Learn a short handshake only you two know
• Whisper three things you’re glad happened today
• Plan a tiny adventure for the weekend

Remember

• Phones can sleep in another room — yours too
• It’s okay if you don’t feel like it at first; short tries count
• You can always come back to the list tomorrow
